To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The chemical and mineralogical compositions of early Llandovery brachiopod bearing sediments from Wales are dominated by chemical enrichment related to original clay and carbonate contents; (2) There are only a few correlations between brachiopods and sediment chemistry/minerals, and these are not strong enough to support any meaningful interpretations.
there is no significant correlation between the chemistry/mineralogy of the sediment and the brachiopod fauna.
the chemical and mineralogical composition of early Llandovery brachiopodbearing sediments in Wales is not correlated with brachiopod species diversity or abundance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) What is the nature of the relationship between sedimentary chemistry and mineralogy, on the one hand, and brachiopod fauna on the other?
the geochemistry and mineralogy (and, in part, the sedimentology) of the early Llandovery sediments, and the relationship between these and the brachiopod fauna.
the geochemistry and mineralogy (in relation to brachioped assemblages) of early Llandovery clastic sediments in Wales.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brachiopod fauna is not related to the chemical and mineralogical composition of the sediments.
the brachiopods of early Llandovery sediments in Wales are not controlled by the sedimentary chemistry or mineralogy.

there is little evidence of a correlation between brachi-opod assemblages and chemistry/mineralogy of early Llandovery sediments in Wales, although there is evidence of some correlation of faunal assemblages with sediment chemistry/mineralology in the Llanvirn.

the Welsh early Llando very sediments are chemically and mineralogically homogeneous, and the observed faunal changes are not controlled by sediment composition.

the chemistry and mineralogy of the sediments are more important than their age and facies in explaining the distribution and diversity of the brachiopod fauna.
